# Sīlavīmaṁsanajātaka (Ja 305)

**ID:** Ja 305
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sīlavīmaṁsanajātaka* (Ja 305), titled in English as "A Test of Virtue," is a canonical Jātaka tale preserved in the Pali Canon. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana regarding the restraint of defilements (*kilesaniggaha*), specifically prompted by five hundred resident monks who had fallen into sensual thoughts during the middle watch of the night [Fausböll 1883]. The commentary notes that the full background story is related in the *Pānīyajātaka* of the Eleventh Book (*Ekādasanipāta*) [Fausböll 1883]. The canonical verse opens with the incipit *N'atthi loke raho nāma* ("There is no secrecy in the world") [Fausböll 1883]. At the end of the exposition, the five hundred monks achieved arahantship, and the Buddha identified the previous births (*samodhāna*), revealing that the teacher of that time was Sāriputta and the wise youth (*paṇḍitamāṇavo*) was the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1883].
